title: The friction-era VOS amplitude of a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ string network from nematic disclination data
summary: A tangle of line defects coarsens as the mean spacing $L$ between neighbouring lines grows. In a viscous medium the motion is overdamped, and the velocity-dependent one-scale (VOS) model predicts a late-time attractor $L^{2}=\mathcal{A}\,\ell_d\,t$, with $\ell_d=T/Γ$ the ratio of line tension to drag and $\mathcal{A}$ a dimensionless amplitude. The growth law $L\propto t^{1/2}$ holds for every value of the three model parameters---the momentum parameter $k\le1$, the sink coefficient $\tilde{c}$, and the curvature ratio $λ\equiv R/L$---since all three enter only through…
